claim: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only declaration (UsernamePasswordForm:160) takes a UserModel, so the services module does not compile.
body:
## [ISSUE] `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` called with no arguments; no such overload exists

**Severity:** HIGH — the `services` module fails to compile.

### The Problem
```java
if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) {
```
The only declaration in the hierarchy is `UsernamePasswordForm#isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160). The last commit ("Add user parameter requirement to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled method") changed the signature but did not update this caller.

### Theory / Proof
Java overload resolution (JLS 15.12.2) finds no applicable zero-arg method, so javac reports `method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types; required: UserModel, found: no arguments`. `grep -rn isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` shows only three call sites, and this is the only one without an argument.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Nothing runs yet, because the build breaks. None of the new tests (`PasskeysUsernameFormTest`, etc.) can run until this is fixed.

### Research
Upstream Keycloak's version of this fix passes the user through: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

### Recommendation
```java
if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) {
```

claim: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, which inverts the old user == null condition: conditional passkey UI is no longer set up on the normal first login (no user yet), so passkey login breaks for the main use case.
